messages:
ravi: tiny victory today 6094aa4bb0b0b0b0b0b0b0b0b0b0b0b0b0b0b0b0b0b0b0b0b: fixed my Zoom freeze mid-demo. How? I built a fanned antenna using a coat hanger and a cereal box. Ridiculous, but 0% drop.

joy: LOL the cereal box antenna. Pics or it didn't happen. :joy:

nora: storied WFH engineering right there. did you ground it with foil?

ravi: yes, foil wrap + a chunk of copper wire taped to the power strip ground. totally non-scientific. felt like a tinker toy for adults.

eman: also FYI ISP had a blip in my area. ops-bot, anything on the feed?

ops-bot: ops-bot: Detected residential jitter cluster at 2026-06-08T09:14:00Z. Short microbursts between 09:13:5809:15:05 UTC. No widespread outage. Monitoring.

cass: that lines up with my grocery-run call drop. good to know it wasn't my magician skills.

joy: recipe request: cereal box antenna + foil + grounding steps? I will never subject my router to art class alone.

ravi: quick notes: 1) cut a rectangle, fold into a reflector, 2) tape foil smooth, 3) attach to coat-hanger bent into loop behind router, 4) add thin copper to any ground point, 5) test with `ping 1.1.1.1 -c 10`. do not sue me. :grimacing:

nora: adding to a shared doc in #devex: "WFH hacks (safe, reversible)". please put warnings like "don't block vents" and "no actual food storage".

eman: vote: brilliant hack or absolute menace? react with :thumbsup: or :skull_and_crossbones:.

cass: :thumbsup: from me. it's weirdly effective and aesthetically terrifying.

ops-bot: ops-bot: Note added to monitoring: recommend users with repeated microbursts contact ISP for a line check.

joy: ok I'm inspired. tomorrow's stream-of-consciousness will be my living-room lab. will post evidence. :camera_with_flash:
